lessons.md:
Open the official AI-103 study guide on Microsoft Learn. Copy every skill it lists into a spreadsheet with three columns: the skill, where you've done it (course or project) and a confidence score from 1 to 3.

Anything scored 1 is your revision list. You've already built much of this outside Azure (RAG, evals, agents, safety); the exam asks how Azure's services do the same jobs. Note the domain weightings: spend time in proportion.

check.q: Your revision list should come from:
o: Skills in the study guide you scored lowest
check.e: Start from the official skills list.

lessons.md:
Work through the Learn paths linked from the study guide, in the guide's order. Habits that save time:

- Skim modules on topics you've built; do the knowledge checks to confirm.
- Slow down on Azure-specific pieces: resource setup, identity and keys, quotas, regions and pricing tiers.
- Keep a one-page sheet of service names and what each is for.

Coursera Plus has Microsoft prep courses if you prefer video; the Learn paths alone are enough.

check.q: Where should you slow down most?
o: Azure-specific setup, identity and service choices

lessons.md:
Reading isn't enough for Azure exams; click through the real thing.

- Create a Foundry project, deploy a model, call it from Python.
- Build an agent with a tool in Foundry.
- Create an Azure AI Search index with vector fields, load your project 1 documents and query it.
- Use managed identity or Key Vault instead of pasting keys.

Set a budget alert first and delete resource groups after each lab.

Microsoft offers a free official practice assessment for its role-based exams. Take it cold, under time, once you've finished the Learn paths.

Then sort every wrong answer by domain. Wrong because you didn't know the service? Add it to your sheet. Misread the question? Note the trap. The practice mode in this portal covers concepts; the official assessment covers Microsoft's question style.

check.q: After the practice assessment, sort wrong answers by:

lessons.md: Revise only weak domains, then retake. Aim for 80% or more on two separate runs before booking. Use spaced review: the portal's practice mode resurfaces questions you missed. Explain each weak concept out loud in two sentences; if you can't, you don't know it yet.

o: You score 80% or more on two practice runs

lessons.md:
Book through Microsoft's exam page: about £106 plus VAT, 120 minutes, pass mark 700 out of 1,000. Online proctored needs a quiet room, a clear desk and ID; a test centre avoids technical risk.

During the exam: flag and move on from slow questions; read every word of case studies; you can usually open Microsoft Learn during role-based exams, but searching costs time, so use it only to confirm. Add the badge to LinkedIn and your CV the day you pass. Renewal is free each year through an online assessment.
